claims.text: A combined high-throughput molecular-dynamics and machine-learning approach can accurately predict melting temperatures of high-entropy alloys.
The combined approach can accurately predict enthalpies of fusion of high-entropy alloys.
The combined approach can accurately predict entropies of fusion of high-entropy alloys.
The combined approach can accurately predict volume changes at melting in high-entropy alloys.
The combined approach can accurately predict liquid-phase thermodynamic properties of high-entropy alloys.
The combined approach is an efficient method for predicting thermodynamic properties across the high-entropy-alloy family.
Atomic-scale disorder governs local structural configurations relevant to melting.
Chemical interactions govern phase transitions in high-entropy alloys.
Molecular-dynamics simulations capture the detailed atomic interactions involved in melting.
Molecular-dynamics simulations capture free-energy changes during melting.
Machine-learning models trained on molecular-dynamics results can generalize thermodynamic relationships to new high-entropy-alloy compositions.
Predicted melting temperatures should agree with experiments within approximately ±50 K.
Predicted fusion enthalpies should agree with experiments within approximately ±10% relative error.
Predicted fusion entropies should agree with experiments within approximately ±10% relative error.
Predicted volume changes at melting should agree with experiments within approximately ±10% relative error.
Predicted key liquid-phase properties should agree with experiments within approximately ±10% relative error.
The approach is primarily applicable to equiatomic or near-equiatomic high-entropy alloys at ambient pressure.
The approach has reduced reliability for off-stoichiometric compositions.
The approach has reduced reliability under extreme thermodynamic conditions.
Controlled temperature ramps minimize kinetic effects during simulations and experiments.
